messages:
maya: Heads-up — customers hitting 429s that don't line up with metering totals. Example: org=acme-corp key=sk_live_ABC123. Enforcer rejects at peak then pipeline ingests events ~30s later and shows the org under quota. :eyes:

arjun: I saw that in the alerts graph, rejections spike then metering catches up. Are we seeing clock skew or late writes?

lina: Billing noticed a small batch of customers showing negative remaining tokens then getting corrected. We're worried about overblocking impacting SLAs.

maya: Related notes: enforcer uses local in-memory lease + Redis cache with 5s TTL. Metering pipeline writes canonical counters to Clickhouse with ~10-40s ingest latency during bursts. If cache expires before CH writeback, we undercount.

sam: Reproduced locally with loadtest: rapid burst -> enforcer TTL expired -> enforcer recomputes from stale cache -> denies even though pipeline will shortly add tokens.

meter-bot: shadow-enforce logs: "deny org=acme-corp reason=stale_local_count ttl_remaining=0 last_write_age=27s". Linking sample trace: https://go/redwood/traces/trace123

arjun: Short-term mitigation ideas: 1) add a server-side grace window (extend by 60s) for keys that were recently reconciled, 2) preferentially read from a low-latency write-through store if last write < 2s, 3) enable shadow-enforce to confirm fixes before full rollback.

maya: Proposed immediate rollout: enable a 45s grace TTL override for burst-capable keys in prod for us-east-1. This is conservative but should cut false-positives by ~80% in my replay. Thoughts?

kev: UX/console implications — we should show "temporary grace applied" on the quota diagnostics page so support teams can see why a request was allowed/denied. Otherwise they'll file tickets.

lina: Billing ask: we need a reconciliation job to mark any artificially-denied tokens so customers don't get double-billed or penalized. If we open a grace window, meter writes may duplicate — we have to dedupe by event id.

sam: Quick detect query to find affected orgs (run in dev first):
```
SELECT org_id, count(*) as denies, max(event_age) as max_age
FROM enforcer.logs
WHERE reason = 'stale_local_count' AND timestamp > now() - interval '1 hour'
GROUP BY org_id
ORDER BY denies DESC
LIMIT 50;
```

arjun: Plan: short-term grace rollout + shadow verification for 48h -> run backfill to replay late events to the canonical counter -> run a reconciliation pass to reconcile any duplicates -> implement long-term fix.

maya: Long-term fix candidates: 1) move to event-sourced counter updates (append-only stream + idempotent apply), 2) make enforcer subscribe to the changefeed and update local caches via pub/sub instead of TTL-only reads, 3) tighten the write path to reduce debounce.

sam: I'll own the short-term toggle and canary. Plan to open a small canary (10% traffic) in us-east-1 tomorrow 09:00 UTC, then 50% after 1 hour if no regression. I'll post rollout notes and a revert command.

lina: I'll draft the reconciliation playbook and a billing-safe dedupe approach (use event_id + origin) and sync with support on the console messaging.

kev: I'll wire a new line on the quota diagnostics page and add an alert when reconciliations exceed X per hour.

arjun: Ops checklist for canary: 
- feature toggle name: `enforcer.grace_window.override`
- canary buckets: 10% us-east-1 -> 50% -> global
- rollback: flip toggle off, clear local caches for canary nodes
- run detection query after each step

maya: Also add a short-term metric: `enforcer.false_deny_rate` (denies where later meter shows available). Need this to evaluate success.

meter-bot: Shadow verdicts will be collected under `shadow.verdicts.ratecap` tag for the next 72h.

sam: I'll post the canary plan doc and the revert command in #eng-releases once ready. Targeting tomorrow.

maya: Thanks — let's coordinate on runbook and set a quick 15m sync 30min before canary. :thumbsup:
